doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Carnegie Hall, bebop and the big bands
title: The family band's King Records session
summary: Brower reads the 1953 session details; Hampton recalls two sides, the 78 release and the personnel.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I have, as your first recording session, a session with Vinson. Is that accurate?
It was in the same company that he was in, but we didn’t record. He was recording for King, also.
You didn’t do a session that had Lonesome Train and Person to Person. Your man says you did. That’s our first . . .

No, I never recorded with Eddie. I would like to have. I know that Eddie was recording with King Records at one time, and we recorded with the family band on King, but we only recorded two sides, because we weren’t really – we didn’t have something that was really valuable enough for them.
This is the sessions – there was April 7th, 1953, Duke Hampton?
Yeah.
The Push, Red Riding Hood Blues, Nasty Man Blues, Please be Good to Me, He’s Mine, Stomp your Feet, Sweet Stuff.
That was all of our compositions, our recordings?
Um-hmm.
Some of them they didn’t release. They only released The Push and something on the other side of that.
So it was a 45, or a . . . ?
It was a vinyl – what you would call those? A 33 or something like that?
78. Vinyl 78.
Do you remember that session?
Sort of. Not really. It was kind of blurred.
Was Thomas Badger part of family?
No. What did he play?
Alto.

Oh yeah. Let’s see now. Who was the Badger? The Badger. That’s what we called him. The Badger. I can’t remember exactly. We did have some friend that we had in the band. One was Thomas Badger, and also Bill Pennick.
Because this group has Alerta Hampton.
Aletra.
Aletra, Marcus “Lucky” Hampton, Carmelita Hampton, Julius “Billy” Brooks?
Yeah, okay. Billy Brooks, a trumpet player.
Yes.
A trumpet player from Cincinnati, Ohio.
Leo Cornett, somebody named [Ira] Ferguson, Russell Hampton. Who was Ferguson?
I’m thinking that Ferguson was – Ferguson, Ferguson. They don’t have any other there for him.
I-l-d – Ild.
Ira Ferguson, trumpet player.
Harry Bell.
Harry Bell I don’t remember.
Played trombone.
Harry Bell. I don’t remember him.
Virtue Hampton . . .
My sister.
. . . Whitted.
Virtue Hampton Whitted. Yeah. She played bass.
Is she somehow related to Ferris Whitted?
No, that was Thomas Whitted that she was married to.
Okay.
Drummer, a very good drummer.
And Dawn Hampton and Calvin Shields.
Calvin Shields, Calvin Shields. What did he play? Drums?
Right.
Calvin Shields, drums. Oh, Eagle Eye. Eagle Eye Shields, a very fine drummer. Played with Lionel Hampton and stayed around Indianapolis most of the time. We had him on this session.
